text:
maya: p99 spike on hosted between 09:12-09:20 UTC, p99 ~1.2s (normal ~160ms). queue depth on router climbed to 120 per shard. Anyone digging?

jake: saw it too, correlates with a burst from tenant:prod-42. rate limiter started throttling then we had backlog.

liam: profiling kernel selector on a few hot servers now. early guess: short-seq kernel mis-select when seq len ~64-80 after recent kselector tweak.

deploy-bot: deploy redwood/runtime@v2.19.0 completed 09:10 UTC by ci-pipeline

sara: hmm deploy at 09:10 could match. changelog mentions 'kselector fallback heuristics'. rolling back to previous selector for a canary to confirm?

jake: logs show increased KV cache evictions during spike. eviction rate jumped from 5/s -> 240/s. that would blow priming and force more weights loads.

liam: attaching quick perf dump (sampled):
```
# hotspot summary
kernel_selector_choose_shortseq  48% cpu
kv_cache_evict_work            22% cpu
queue_coalesce_wait           15% cpu
batch_builder_padding        10% cpu
```

liam: also saw that batch size distribution skewed: lots of single-request batches appearing after evictions, so throughput falls and p99 climbs.

maya: ops-bot, any noisy neighbor alerts from infra during 09:10-09:25?

ops-bot: Detected GPU memory pressure on host-gpu-17 at 09:11, tenant prod-88 had a large allocation spike. Marked noisy-tenant=prod-88. Throttle policies applied.

sara: so two contributing factors: kselector change + noisy tenant causing extra kv churn. plan: 1) revert kselector tweak on canary, 2) temporarily tighten tenant isolation on noisy-tenant, 3) add shortseq affinity backstop in selector.

jake: I've staged a canary rollback on 3 hosts (hosts: gpu-17,gpu-18,gpu-19). rolling back now.

deploy-bot: rollback redwood/runtime@v2.18.9 triggered by jake at 09:28 UTC

liam: after rollback canary p95/p99 on those hosts dropped back to baseline within 45s. eviction rate back to ~6/s.

maya: good signal. let's track for 30m and follow up on kselector heuristic and KV cache prefetching tuning.

sara: will open a follow-up ticket: RFC to add a metric for 'kselector_mismatch_rate' and an automated canary guard that blocks selector changes when kv_eviction_rate > 50/s. assigning to liam/jake.

liam: noted. quick triage notes saved to incident doc.

jake: TL;DR: regression on selector heuristics + noisy tenant memory pressure -> KV churn -> batch frag -> p99 spike. mitigated by rollback + tenant throttling.

maya: thanks all. I'll ping infra to continue noisy-tenant isolation and ops to update runbook. :thumbsup:
